<a id="makeraudiolength"></a>

## `MakerAudioLength`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Catalog.MakerAudioLength` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The length of a pack's voice file, read from its headers without decoding any audio: a WAV's `fmt` and `data` chunks, an Ogg Vorbis file's identification header and the granule position of its last page. Used for [`MakerLine.DubDurationSec`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.md#makerline--dubdurationsec).

Only the two formats the voice feature loads (`.wav`, `.ogg` Vorbis). Anything else, and any header that does not add up (for a WAV also a second `fmt` or `data` chunk), is "unknown" (false) rather than a guess. No checksum is verified: this answers "how long", not "is it valid", which the loader decides when it loads.

<a id="makeraudiolength--longtail"></a>

### `const int LongTail = 67584`

The longest an Ogg page can be (27 + 255 + 255 x 255), plus slack.

<a id="makeraudiolength--shorttail"></a>

### `const int ShortTail = 8192`

The first tail read when looking for the last Ogg page.

<a id="makeraudiolength--tryoggvorbis"></a>

### `static bool TryOggVorbis(Stream stream, out double seconds)`

The length of an Ogg Vorbis stream: the granule position (samples) of its last page over the sample rate in its identification header.

**Parameters**

- `stream`: A readable, seekable stream positioned anywhere.
- `seconds`: The length in seconds, rounded to the millisecond.

**Returns:** False for another codec (Opus, FLAC) or a header that does not add up.

<a id="makeraudiolength--tryread"></a>

### `static bool TryRead(string path, out double seconds)`

Reads a file's length by its extension (`.wav` or `.ogg`).

**Parameters**

- `path`: An absolute file path.
- `seconds`: The length in seconds, rounded to the millisecond.

**Returns:** False when the file is missing, unreadable, not one of the two formats, or its header does not add up.

<a id="makeraudiolength--trywav"></a>

### `static bool TryWav(Stream stream, out double seconds)`

The length of a RIFF/WAVE stream: `data` bytes over (sample rate x block align).

**Parameters**

- `stream`: A readable, seekable stream positioned anywhere.
- `seconds`: The length in seconds, rounded to the millisecond.

**Returns:** False when the headers are missing or do not add up.

<a id="makercatalogview"></a>

## `MakerCatalogView`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Catalog.MakerCatalogView` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The catalog's answers, from one game snapshot and one read of the packs: the line list with search, filters and paging, one line, and the pack list. No Unity and no game types, so every rule is unit-tested; the adapter (`Bulbul/Maker/MakerCatalog`) only supplies the inputs.

Where each [`MakerLine`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.md#makerline) field comes from:

- **Id, Voice, Ja, En**: the game's `LocalizationMaster` row (packs' `data/localization.json` overrides included, as injected).
- **Group**: the `ScenarioGroupID` of the first `NovelMaster` row that names the line, else the group or source it was last spoken from; [`MakerLineRules.OmittedGroup`](#makerlinerules--omittedgroup) for an omitted line.
- **DurationSec**: the game's own clip length from the voice manager's cache, else the length seen when the game played its own clip; null for an omitted line.
- **Subtitle, SubtitlePack**: the last loaded pack whose `data/subtitles/<lang>.json` has a non-empty entry for the id.
- **DubPack, DubDurationSec**: the pack whose `audio/voice/<lang>/<voice>.wav|.ogg` the voice feature would play, and that file's length from its header.

Thread-safe: everything it holds is immutable or (the two caches) locked.

## `MakerDlcGate`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Catalog.MakerDlcGate` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Pack Maker's DLC gate: decides from the game's scenario data which lines are paid DLC content, and hides them unless the player is known to own that DLC. Unity-free; the adapter passes it to [`MakerGameData`](#makergamedata), which drops the hidden rows, novel rows and groups at capture, so every catalog, editor, export and count reads the gated snapshot.

Fail closed: a marker stays active unless its app is [`MakerDlcOwnership.Owned`](#makerdlcownership--owned); a missing ownership function, an exception or [`MakerDlcOwnership.Unknown`](#makerdlcownership--unknown) all hide. A line spoken by a free group and a DLC group is hidden. While a type marker is active, a group the gate cannot classify (missing from the group list, or of unknown type) is hidden (audit IG-02). When the running game is newer than [`MakerDlcMarkers.MadeForGameVersion`](#makerdlcmarkers--madeforgameversion), or its version is unknown, every line that no classified group speaks is hidden too (audit F1); lines of groups classified free stay listed. No network and no Steam call is made here; the ownership function is the host's.

<a id="makerdlcgate--ctor-ienumerable-makerdlcmarker-func-uint-makerdlcownership"></a>

### `MakerDlcGate(IEnumerable<MakerDlcMarker> markers, Func<uint, MakerDlcOwnership> ownership)`

Creates a gate that does not know the running game's version (treated as a build the markers were not made for).

**Parameters**

- `markers`: The markers; null entries are dropped. Null or empty = nothing is DLC.
- `ownership`: Ownership per Steam app id; null = unknown for every app (hide).

<a id="makerdlcgate--ctor-ienumerable-makerdlcmarker-func-uint-makerdlcownership-func-string-string"></a>

### `MakerDlcGate(IEnumerable<MakerDlcMarker> markers, Func<uint, MakerDlcOwnership> ownership, Func<string> gameVersion, string madeFor)`

Creates a gate that compares the running game's version with the build the markers were made for.

**Parameters**

- `markers`: The markers; null entries are dropped. Null or empty = nothing is DLC.
- `ownership`: Ownership per Steam app id; null = unknown for every app (hide).
- `gameVersion`: The running game's version (normally `Application.version`); null, blank, unreadable or throwing = unknown.
- `madeFor`: The build the markers were made for; null = [`MakerDlcMarkers.MadeForGameVersion`](#makerdlcmarkers--madeforgameversion).

<a id="makerdlcgate--madefor"></a>

The game build the markers were made for.

## `MakerDlcMarkers`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Catalog.MakerDlcMarkers` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The DLC markers the loader ships. Code, not configuration: a list a user could empty would be a way around the gate, so only a loader release changes it, and adding a marker only ever hides more.

<a id="makerdlcmarkers--dlcscenariotype"></a>

### `const int DlcScenarioType = 3`

`Bulbul.MasterData.ScenarioType.DLCScenario`: the game's own type for DLC stories (no group used it in 1.17.3).

<a id="makerdlcmarkers--madeforgameversion"></a>

### `const string MadeForGameVersion = "1.18.1"`

The game build these markers were made for ([`GameVersionGate.ExpectedGameVersion`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.md#gameversiongate--expectedgameversion)). On a newer or unreadable build the gate hides every line no classified group speaks (audit F1) until a loader release confirms the new build.

<a id="makerdlcmarkers--roomexpansionappid"></a>

### `const uint RoomExpansionAppId = 3718890`

Steam app id of the game's DLC constant `NestopiSystem.Steam.BulbulSteamDLC.DLC_1` (read in 1.17.3). The Steam store lists app 3718890 as the "Room & Cozy Activities Expansion" (HN-056, 2026-11-14; not verified by the loader).

<a id="makerdlcmarkers--all"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<MakerDlcMarker> All { get; }`

[`MakerDlcMarkers.BuiltIn`](#makerdlcmarkers--builtin) then [`MakerDlcMarkers.DlcDay`](#makerdlcmarkers--dlcday).

<a id="makerdlcmarkers--builtin"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<MakerDlcMarker> BuiltIn { get; }`

Always on: every group of the game's own DLC story type is DLC.

<a id="makerdlcmarkers--dlcday"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<MakerDlcMarker> DlcDay { get; }`

The DLC's own groups and lines, filled when the DLC ships (24 Nov 2026) from that build's master data. Empty until then.

## `MakerGameData`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Catalog.MakerGameData` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What the catalog reads from the running game, taken in one go on the main thread: the localisation rows in the game's own order, the lengths of the game's voice clips, and the voice names mods and packs registered at runtime. Immutable; the catalog serves every query from one of these until something invalidates it.

<a id="makergamedata--ctor-ienumerable-makergamerow-ireadonlydictionary-string-double-ienumerable-string-ienumerable-makergamenovelrow-ienumerable-makergamegroup-string"></a>

<a id="makerlinerules"></a>

## `MakerLineRules`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Catalog.MakerLineRules` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The rules the Pack Maker catalog (ticket DS-02) applies to one line in one language: what it needs, what it has, which `filter` it belongs to, and whether a search matches it.

**Omitted lines.** The game data carries rows the game never speaks: ids ending in [`MakerLineRules.OmitSuffix`](#makerlinerules--omitsuffix) (game 1.18.0 has 15, whose voice names have no clip), and any voiced row whose clip exists nowhere - not in the game's voice cache, not registered by a mod, not in any pack. They are listed under `all` (last, with [`MakerLine.Group`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.md#makerline--group) set to [`MakerLineRules.OmittedGroup`](#makerlinerules--omittedgroup) so a UI can hide them), need neither a subtitle nor a dub, and so never appear under `missing-subtitle`, `missing-dub` or `done`.

**Needs.** A line needs a subtitle when the game has text for it (Japanese or English not blank) and a dub when it has a voice name. The game's wordless vocalisations (motion grunts: a voice, no text) therefore need a dub and no subtitle.

**Has.** A subtitle counts when it is not empty: the game's text seam treats an empty table entry as no entry and falls back along the language's chain, so an empty entry would show the fallback text in the game.

**Not listed at all:** rows `Satone.Say` adds at runtime ([`MakerLineRules.IsRuntimeRow`](#makerlinerules--isruntimerow)).

<a id="makerlinerules--filterall"></a>

### `const string FilterAll = "all"`

The `filter` value for [`MakerLineFilter.All`](#makerlinefilter--all).

<a id="makerlinerules--filterdone"></a>

### `const string FilterDone = "done"`

The `filter` value for [`MakerLineFilter.Done`](#makerlinefilter--done).

<a id="makerlinerules--filtermissingdub"></a>

### `const string FilterMissingDub = "missing-dub"`

The `filter` value for [`MakerLineFilter.MissingDub`](#makerlinefilter--missingdub).

<a id="makerlinerules--filtermissingsubtitle"></a>

### `const string FilterMissingSubtitle = "missing-subtitle"`

The `filter` value for [`MakerLineFilter.MissingSubtitle`](#makerlinefilter--missingsubtitle).

<a id="makerlinerules--langpattern"></a>

The largest page (`limit`).

<a id="makerlinerules--minlimit"></a>

## `MakerPackContent`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Catalog.MakerPackContent` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What the loaded packs hold on disk right now for Pack Maker: every subtitle table with the pack each entry comes from, and every language voice set with the pack each clip comes from. Built by [`MakerPackScanner.Scan`](#makerpackscanner--scan); immutable.

Read from disk rather than from the game's merged tables because the merged tables have lost which pack each entry came from, and because Pack Maker's own saves land on disk first. The rules are the game's own: subtitle tables by [`SubtitleTables.LanguageOf`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.MasterData.md#subtitletables--languageof), later pack over earlier; voice sets by [`LanguageVoicePlan`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Voice.md#languagevoiceplan) (folder codes normalised, later pack over earlier, later path over earlier within a pack).

<a id="makerpackrules"></a>

## `MakerPackRules`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Catalog.MakerPackRules` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

CONTRACT.md "Editable packs": a pack is editable when it is a content pack (no `entryDll`) in `CWYLS Mods`, loaded this session, whose folder is writable, and which is not a reference pack. The first rule a pack fails is its reason.

**Reference packs** are the example and demo packs this repository ships in `packs/` (`cwy.example`, `cwy.demo.*`, `cwy.sample.*`): `deploy-packs.sh` replaces their folders wholesale, so an edit made in them would be lost on the next deploy.

**Links (DS-10a).** A pack whose `data/subtitles` or `audio/voice` folder is, or goes through, a symbolic link or junction is read-only: Pack Maker never reads or writes through a link, because a link can point anywhere outside the pack. The pack folder itself is not checked (the loader loaded it from there; the editor's own path rule starts below it too).

<a id="makerpackrules--codemodreason"></a>

### `const string CodeModReason = "It is a code mod (entryDll); Pack Maker writes to content packs only."`

Reason: the pack is a code mod.

<a id="makerpackrules--notloadedreason"></a>

### `const string NotLoadedReason = "It did not load this session: "`

Reason: the pack was found but did not load this session (the detail follows).

<a id="makerpackrules--notwritablereason"></a>

### `const string NotWritableReason = "Its folder is read-only."`

Reason: the pack folder cannot be written to.

<a id="makerpackrules--outsidepacksrootreason"></a>

### `const string OutsidePacksRootReason = "It is not in the CWYLS Mods folder."`

Reason: the pack folder is not a folder of `CWYLS Mods`.

<a id="makerpackrules--referencepackreason"></a>

### `const string ReferencePackReason = "It is a reference pack that ships with the loader and is replaced on every deploy; copy it to a pack of your own."`

Reason: the pack is one of the loader's reference packs.

<a id="makerpackrules--contentfolders"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<string> ContentFolders { get; }`

The pack folders Pack Maker reads and writes, pack-relative with forward slashes.

<a id="makerpackrules--referencepackids"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<string> ReferencePackIds { get; }`

<a id="makerpackrules--referencepackprefixes"></a>

<a id="makerpackscanner"></a>

## `MakerPackScanner`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Catalog.MakerPackScanner` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Reads the loaded packs' subtitle tables and voice files off disk into a [`MakerPackContent`](#makerpackcontent), and fingerprints those folders cheaply so the catalog can tell when to read them again.

Only two places of a pack are read: `data/subtitles/*.json` (direct children) and `audio/voice/` (its files and its direct sub-folders' files). Hidden files (`.DS_Store`, `._x.ogg`) are ignored. Nothing is written.

**Links (DS-10a).** Nothing is read through a symbolic link or junction, so nothing outside the pack folder is: a linked table, clip or language folder is skipped, and a `data/subtitles` or `audio/voice` folder that is (or goes through) a link is not read at all. Each skip is one line in [`MakerPackContent.Problems`](#makerpackcontent--problems), which the catalog logs; [`MakerPackRules.Decide`](#makerpackrules--decide) reports such a pack read-only.

**Fingerprint.** Per pack: the last write time of `data/subtitles/` and the size and last write time of each table in it, and the last write time of `audio/voice/` and of each folder in it. A save that adds, removes or atomically replaces a file changes its folder's time; a table edited in place changes its own. A clip overwritten in place is not seen here (the set is unchanged); its new length is, because lengths are keyed by the file's own time ([`MakerDubLengths`](#makerdublengths)).

<a id="makerpackscanner--fingerprint"></a>

### `static string Fingerprint(IEnumerable<MakerPackSource> packs)`

A cheap description of the folders [`MakerPackScanner.Scan`](#makerpackscanner--scan) reads, for change detection.

**Parameters**

- `packs`: The packs, in load order; packs that did not load are skipped.

<a id="makerpackscanner--scan"></a>

### `static MakerPackContent Scan(IEnumerable<MakerPackSource> packs, string fingerprint = null)`

Reads the packs' subtitle tables and voice files.

**Parameters**

- `packs`: The packs, in load order; packs that did not load are skipped.
- `fingerprint`: The [`MakerPackScanner.Fingerprint`](#makerpackscanner--fingerprint) taken before reading; null takes one now. Taking it first means a file changed during the read makes the next fingerprint differ, so it is read again.

## `MakerPlayedLines`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Catalog.MakerPlayedLines` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Which line a Pack Maker Play started: Play speaks through `Satone.Say`, so the game reports the runtime row it added (`cwy_say_*`), which the catalog does not list. This remembers the last few runtime rows Play queued and the line each one came from, so `line.spoken` can name the line (its `lineId` field). Safe from any thread.

<a id="makerplayedlines--maxentries"></a>

### `const int MaxEntries = 32`

The most plays remembered; the oldest is forgotten first.

<a id="makerplayedlines--lineid"></a>

### `string LineId(string localizationId)`

The catalog line a spoken row stands for: the line Play started for a runtime row it queued, null for any other runtime row (another mod's `Satone.Say`), and the row id itself for a game row.

**Parameters**

- `localizationId`: The row id `line.spoken` reports, or null.

<a id="makerplayedlines--note"></a>

### `void Note(string runtimeId, string lineId)`

Records that Play queued `runtimeId` to say `lineId`.

**Parameters**

- `runtimeId`: The runtime row id, e.g. `cwy_say_12_001`. Blank is ignored.
- `lineId`: The catalog line it plays. Blank is ignored.

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Catalog.MakerSpokenCache` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What the catalog learns from lines the game really speaks (`line.spoken`): the length of the game's own clip for a voice, and the scenario group or source a row was spoken from. The second source for [`MakerLine.DurationSec`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.md#makerline--durationsec) and [`MakerLine.Group`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.md#makerline--group) when the snapshot does not know them. Safe from any thread.
